newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: PALM OIL-S.E. Asian palm oil seen up on currency.
newsitem.headline: PALM OIL-S.E. Asian palm oil seen up on currency.

text.p: Southeast Asian palm oil prices are expected to rise this week to offset weakness in the Malaysian ringgit and Indonesian rupiah, regional traders said.
Strong demand was also expected to boost sentiment.

"It will be a currency market this week. If the rupiah weakens further against the U.S. dollar, prices will have to be adjusted higher," an Indonesian trader said. "Otherwise, players will just export their oil because of better prices overseas."
Regional players are also closely watching the ringgit's movement against the dollar. The ringgit fell to a historical low of 2.8250 to the dollar last Friday.
"Palm oil is likely to move up further this week if the ringgit stays weak, and local prices will be very competitive against Indonesian palm," a Kuala Lumpur trader said.
The rupiah fell to a historic low of 2,960 to the dollar on Friday in reaction to the central bank decision to scrap its intervention band on Thursday.
"The lower rupiah will make exports more competitive. But local prices will have to adjust to export prices, otherwise there will be no interest in the market," said another Indonesian trader.
Indonesian palm olein ended last week at 1,570 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, up from 1,470-75 rupiah the previous week.

On Friday, Malaysia's benchmark third-month October futures closed at 1,269 ringgit a tonne, against 1,220 a week earlier. It is expected to test immediate resistance of 1,280, before heading for the 1,300 psychological level.
"I was friendly before and I'm even more friendly to the market now. We could see another rally this week," the general manager of a trading house in Singapore said.

A fall in end-July palm stocks, released by Malaysia's Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA), to 769,275 tonnes from 789,806 tonnes at the end of June looks "pretty positive" for the market, he said.
Traders said palm oil prices were getting a boost from strong offtake from India and China.
"It's looking good. China has been taking a superb number of imports," a dealer in Singapore said.
Singapore dealers said the only cloud hovering over the market was the fact that output remains robust.
The peak production period in Malaysia is coming up and fears over a possible slowdown in export offtake in the next few months may then hit prices, they said.
"People may say that production is running great and take that as a bearish signal," said one dealer.

PORLA said exports in July soared to 715,906 tonnes against 622,210 tonnes in June. Cargo surveyor SGS (M) Sdn Bhd estimated first-half August palm oil exports in Malaysia at 312,757 tonnes against 307,536 tonnes for July 1-15.
"Production is going to be excellent. People are asking if China and India can maintain the strong offtake they've shown lately," one trader said.
"My bias is slightly upward, maybe by about 10 ringgit in the Kuala Lumpur Commodity Exchange (KLCE)," another Singapore-based dealer said.
